title: Historical V54 - Gmail Integration Architecture
summary: How Gmail routes, services, stores, sync, capability planning, and confirmation gates fit into the SMTO runtime.
html:
Historical reference. See the current V55 architecture guide before using this material.

Gmail Integration Architecture

Gmail is an integration subsystem, not a replacement execution path. It keeps the core SMTO boundary intact: the LLM proposes meaning, the runtime validates typed contracts and safety, and a dedicated service touches the external system.

flowchart TD UI[Agent UI Gmail drawer and Mail workspace] --> R[FastAPI Gmail routes] R --> S[GmailService] S --> DB[(agent_gmail.db)] S --> G[Google Gmail API] R --> C[gmail.agent capability] C --> L[LLM structured calls] C --> V[Runtime validation and confirmation] V --> S S --> SYNC[GmailSyncManager] SYNC --> DB

Components

Component Responsibility
route_groups/gmail.py Browser API routes, request payload models, HTTP error mapping, prompt helpers, and account-aware route calls.
gmail/service.py OAuth, Gmail REST calls, local cache coordination, draft/send/mutation operations, prompt search helpers, and account resolution.
gmail/store.py SQLite schema, account records, message metadata, labels, attachments, sender inventory, drafts, sync state, and events.
gmail/sync.py Background polling, manual sync, cancellation, stale state recovery, and label backfill.
capabilities/gmail.py LLM-owned Gmail intent selection, semantic matching, analysis reports, mutation previews, unsubscribe handling, and confirmation replay.
Agent UI static files Gmail drawer, Mail workspace, account selector, labels, thread detail, composer, reminder popups, and queue/ledger panels.

Data Model

The Gmail store is local SQLite state. It stores:

  • connected accounts and OAuth tokens;
  • browser-safe account summaries;
  • cached message metadata;
  • cached labels and attachment summaries;
  • normalized senders for sender search and reports;
  • draft metadata;
  • per-account sync state;
  • bounded sync events.

account_id scopes cache rows and sync state. User-facing payloads can use account_ref, which the service resolves against account id, email, display name, nickname, and primary-account state.

Request Flow

sequenceDiagram participant UI as Mail UI participant API as Gmail Routes participant Cap as gmail.agent participant Runtime participant Service as GmailService participant Google as Gmail API UI->>API: Prompt or selected-thread action API->>Cap: Structured Gmail request context Cap->>Runtime: Typed intent, selector, operation Runtime->>Runtime: Validate account, scope, risk, confirmation Runtime->>Service: Read, draft, preview, or confirmed mutation Service->>Google: Gmail REST call when needed Google-->>Service: Gmail response Service-->>API: Safe response payload API-->>UI: Result, preview, draft, or confirmation state

Read-only flows can answer from cache or bounded fetched thread context. Mutation flows create previews and confirmation payloads before execution. Sending a draft is a mutation.

Sync Flow

The sync manager warms the local cache without making the cache trusted authority. Gmail remains the source for message state. The cache exists to make the UI responsive, support sender and label navigation, and bound model context.

Sync behavior:

  • manual sync can target one account or all connected accounts;
  • background sync runs only when enabled and connected accounts exist;
  • sync state is per account;
  • stale in-flight state is reset on backend startup;
  • label backfill can be queued when a UI view needs metadata that is not warm;
  • Pub/Sub helpers decode Gmail notifications when optional watch settings are configured.

Safety And Confirmation

The capability treats broad email changes as high-impact because they alter real mail state. The preview and confirmation payload should include enough evidence for the user to understand the account, operation, selected messages, batch size, and likely effect.

The LLM may classify, summarize, draft, and select likely matches. It does not own:

  • OAuth token storage;
  • account trust;
  • mutation approval;
  • Gmail API execution;
  • cache schema migration;
  • final send authority.

Current runtime validation, account resolution, Gmail service errors, and user approval remain authoritative even when a semantic match looks confident.

Maintainer Notes

When adding Gmail behavior:

  • keep request/response models strict with extra="forbid";
  • accept account_ref on new account-scoped routes and payloads;
  • keep full message bodies bounded and selected-context only;
  • prefer previews over direct mutations;
  • include sync/cache state in user-facing status rather than hiding delays;
  • update Gmail Integration and System Surfaces And API Reference whenever routes or safety behavior change.
